title: PowerPoint on the web: Copilot Agent Mode can reference SharePoint and OneDrive files named in a prompt
summary: The briefing's availability, permissions, licensing qualifications and governance controls are supported. The statement that presentation creation produces a new file needs an additional Microsoft citation; no blocking correction was found.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes referencing files when creating a presentation using Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint recognizes SharePoint and OneDrive files mentioned by name in a presentation-creation prompt.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Copilot can use the named file as context for creating the presentation.
claims.quote: You can naturally reference a relevant file in your prompt, and Copilot can use that file as context when creating your presentation.

claims.claim: Implicit file references previously were not supported for files in these locations.
claims.quote: Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations.

claims.claim: Users need not manually attach or upload the referenced file first.
claims.quote: This update makes it easier to use relevant Microsoft 365 content without manually attaching or uploading the file.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The release note groups roadmap items 555894, 555895 and 555897 under the same Copilot in PowerPoint feature.
claims.quote:

555894
555895

claims.claim: The release note lists Windows, Mac and Web.
claims.quote: Reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint [Windows, Mac, Web]

claims.claim: Learn places the feature among updates released between September 22, 2026, and October 06, 2026.
claims.quote:
October 06, 2026
Updates released between September 22, 2026, and October 06, 2026.

claims.claim: Copilot features gradually reach a subset of tenant users before expanding across the organization.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot references content under the user's existing permissions rather than granting new access.
claims.quote: Permissions come first. Copilot only summarizes or references content that the user is already authorized to access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can surface already-overshared SharePoint and OneDrive content to users who have access.
claims.quote: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions. If content is already overshared, Copilot can surface it to anyone who has access.

claims.claim: The presentation workflow can use the reference without the user first locating the file.
claims.quote: You can bring existing SharePoint and OneDrive content into your presentation workflow more naturally, without first locating the file and manually attaching it.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: users invoke it by naming a file in their prompt.
claims.quote: In your prompt, reference a file saved in SharePoint or OneDrive by the document name and/or owner of the document.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No setting specific to turning implicit file references in PowerPoint on or off was documented in the sources searched.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot PowerPoint implicit file references SharePoint OneDrive admin disable setting PowerShell policy' and 'Copilot in PowerPoint file references admin control turn off implicit SharePoint OneDrive Microsoft Graph cloud policy'; read the release-note entry and Copilot overview.

claims.claim: The generated presentation is a new file built from referenced content.
claims.quote:
Copilot generates the new presentation in a new file when starting from an existing presentation [Web]
Now, when creating a presentation using Copilot from an existing presentation, it creates the new presentation in a new file without affecting the original presentation.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/previous-year-release-notes#september-30,-2025 to sources for the new-file statement.

claims.claim: New content created by Copilot in PowerPoint inherits the source file's sensitivity label and its protection settings.
claims.quote: If you use Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook to create new content based on an item that has a sensitivity label applied, the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.

claims.claim: When multiple files supply new content, the highest-priority sensitivity label is inherited.
claims.quote: If multiple files are used to create new content, the sensitivity label with the highest priority is used for label inheritance.

claims.claim: Label inheritance is not supported for content encrypted with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Label inheritance isn't supported for content encrypted with user-defined permissions.

claims.claim: Copilot presents only data the individual can access through the underlying Microsoft 365 access controls.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: The release-note entry does not identify which component fetches the referenced file.
claims.quote: Searched: the release-note entry for 555894, 555895 and 555897, including What changed, Why, Try this and impact paragraphs; it describes naming a document and using its content, without naming a fetching component.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A sensitivity-label DLP rule on the Copilot policy location can exclude labelled content from processing in Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: This feature is available in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork, and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Items excluded by sensitivity-label DLP still appear in citations without their content being used in the response.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.claim: The release-note entry describes no background, scheduled or source-file write action.
claims.quote: Searched: the complete release-note entry for 555894, 555895 and 555897; its steps are to start creating a presentation, reference a file in a prompt and ask for a presentation using that file. No background, scheduled or source-file write action is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: DLP policy changes can take up to four hours to reach Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Updates to a DLP policy can take up to four hours to reflect in the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork experiences.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes require propagation time.
claims.quote: Because the setting must propagate across indexing systems, updates can take time to become fully effective.

claims.claim: The roadmap and release-note entry name no feature-specific licence tier, meter or charge.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot PowerPoint reference SharePoint OneDrive files Microsoft 365 Copilot Basic license meter pricing'; read the roadmap record, full release-note entry and Copilot overview. Neither the record nor the entry specifies a licence tier, meter or charge.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence provides the full Copilot experience in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic), unlike Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic), does not provide Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license and don't have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Some Copilot features are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint has mixed licensing experiences, with Basic access without the add-on and a full add-on tier.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the full add-on licensed experience (some features are subject to fair use limits), which includes everything in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The release-note entry does not distinguish entitlement for implicit SharePoint and OneDrive file references.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot in PowerPoint implicit file references pricing meter license Basic Premium'; read the full feature entry and Copilot overview. The entry gives no Basic/Premium distinction; the overview describes app tiers without naming implicit file references.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires Copilot licensing and SharePoint Advanced Management availability.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: The Copilot DLP page refers licensing questions to Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans and Microsoft 365 Service Descriptions.
claims.quote:
For information on licensing, see
- Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans
- Microsoft 365 Service Descriptions

claims.claim: User licences are managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page.
Select the row of the user that you want to unassign a license for.
In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps.
Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense adds or removes user licences.
claims.quote:
Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to.
POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/assignLicense

claims.claim: The assignLicense request body's removeLicenses collection identifies licences to remove.
claims.quote: removeLicenses | Guid collection | A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is configured at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is site-level and applies to SharePoint sites, not OneDrive sites.
claims.quote:
Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.
You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability rather than existing user permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences operating on content already in use by the user.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: The documentation does not state whether a file named in a PowerPoint prompt falls under Restricted Content Discovery or its content-in-use exception.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Restricted Content Discovery PowerPoint file named prompt reference explicit files' and '"Restricted Content Discovery" "reference" "PowerPoint"'; read the RCD page and release-note entry. Neither classifies this named-file workflow.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: The Purview route Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork selects the Copilot policy location.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot example uses New-DlpComplianceRule with Name, Policy, AdvancedRule and RestrictAccess setting ExcludeContentProcessing with value Block.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The Copilot example first creates its policy with New-DlpCompliancePolicy and EnforcementPlanes set to CopilotExperiences.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The label-exclusion rule uses the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition.
claims.quote: create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.claim: The sensitivity-label DLP rule covers stored file items and items actively open.
claims.quote:
A rule configured to protect items with sensitivity labels applies to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork and supports the following content:
- File items, which are stored and items that are actively open.

claims.claim: In Word, Excel and PowerPoint, this DLP policy is evaluated at file open.
claims.quote: In Word, Excel, and PowerPoint the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy to prevent Copilot from processing content is evaluated at file open.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label applied mid-session affects DLP enforcement the next time the file is opened.
claims.quote: If a sensitivity label is applied mid-session, the policy will be enforced starting the next time the file is opened.

claims.claim: The Copilot DLP policy can be run in simulation mode.
claims.quote: Policy simulation mode is available for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork.

claims.claim: The sources checked do not establish whether removing the add-on licence removes this specific implicit-file-reference capability.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot in PowerPoint implicit file references pricing meter license Basic Premium'; read the release-note entry, Copilot overview and assignLicense reference. They distinguish app licence tiers and licence removal but do not assign this capability to a tier.
